programmes.d: A dismembered body is dumped on the side of the New Jersey Turnpike.
While investigating the murder of 9-year-old Jessica Knott, police use a garbage bag to connect suspect James Edward Crow, Jr. to the crime.
A young bride-to-be is gunned down and investigators uncover the man she loved was living a lie.

When four-month-old Ryan Stallings dies under suspicious circumstances, his mother is ultimately convicted of his murder. But months later, new evidence emerges from a startling source — his newborn brother.
Tara Munsey went missing after a work shift at a Virginia restaurant.

When a decomposed body is found stuffed in a barrel, it's easy to presume murder. But the body had been placed in the barrel 30 years earlier. One of the few clues was an address book found along with the body.
An Ohio woman and her two daughters go missing while vacationing in Florida.

A fifteen-year-old boy dies from a mysterious gunshot wound to the head while sitting in the lobby of his father's gun club. Ballistics, laser technology, made-to-scale models and the latest in forensic animation are used to find the cause.
Four young adults are murdered in an affluent Texas neighborhood, with little evidence.
In 1995, when off-duty Maine State Trooper Vicky Gardner is attacked by Steven Fortin during a routine stop, it triggers a chain of events which jumpstart a stalled murder case in New Jersey.
In 2008, college co-ed Jenna Verhaalen was found dead in her Bryan, Texas apartment.

When a popular gym teacher is found dead of what appears to be an accidental gunshot wound, his family is suspicious. A tape recorded by the victim just before his death tells the true story of his strange marriage and his wife's insatiable greed.
A woman and her soon-to-be ex-husband are murdered shortly after she meets a man online.
Young Navajos in the Southwest were dying at an alarming rate. The tribe's medicine men provided investigators with a critical clue that would lead halfway around the world to a most unlikely killer.
In 2003, Kathy Lorick was murdered on a Concord, California jogging trail in the middle of the day.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers. An investigator reveals that their ill health is due to mold in their modern home.
All evidence leads to the wife when a real estate developer is murdered.

On May 20, 2001, Carrie Nelson was beaten to death while working alone in a park office. The case went unsolved for six years. Finally, police found a match with DNA samples gathered from the crime scene.
In 2005, the body of young mother Summer Baldwin was found in a suitcase in a Texas landfill.
In 2004, nursing student Tamika Huston went missing from her Spartanburg, South Carolina home.

In 1971, John List left a note with the bodies of his mother, wife and three children in his mansion ballroom before disappearing completely. Detectives must solve the case, despite having only an outdated photograph of List.
In 2002, funeral director Lonnie Turner, Sr. was found shot to death.

Police investigate a discarded sleeping bag containing bloody sneakers and a purse, which eventually leads to the body of a young woman. A mark found on the victim's body enables police to track the killer.
Series premiere. A flight attendant went missing and was never seen again.

When hunters reported finding a skull in a Texas canyon, police immediately began an investigation. With a forensic artist's reconstruction, police eventually learned the victim's identity. Now all they had to do was find her killer.
Old-fashioned police work and computer animation determine how a 15-year-old boy was shot.
Two sets of scientists probe a woman's death.
A woman disappeared and her husband became the prime suspect.

A man disappears one year to the day after beginning an affair with his friend's wife. 15 years later, with the help of a metal detector, police find evidence that would prove what had happened and who was responsible.
In 1986, scientists and detectives use DNA to solve a string of rapes and murders in the UK.

When a 9-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her. A psychic's vision leads to a field where her body is discovered, along with what investigators hope is enough evidence to find her killer.
Police use DNA profiles of seed pods from a truck to catch a killer.

In 1996, police received a call from Darlie Routier telling them of her two sons' murders. The police found the killer by analyzing blood spatter, doing behavioral profiling and analyzing Darlie's 911 call.
With the use of DNA profiling, an innocent man is freed and the real killer is convicted.
In 1996, 54-year-old Gayle Isleib was ambushed in her Manchester, Connecticut driveway and shot to death. Police had to determine whether obsessive love was the motive for her murder.
When 182 war veterans contract pneumonia-like symptoms in Philadelphia, doctors become stumped.
A highway patrolman was dispatched to what he thought would be a routine traffic accident — until he looked in the car. He had seen hundreds of accidents, but none with as much blood as this.
On the night of May 22, 1992, Betty Wilson discovered her husband lying in a pool of blood.
Even though their daughter had run away before, she had always come back. Her parents were sure this time would be no different, but they were wrong.
Investigators solve the 1988 murder of a drifter by examining a species of fly found near the body.
In 1993, 82-year-old Kathryn Bishop was found dead in her Pennsylvania home. Tiny clues on the victim's body would tell police what happened that night.
In 1985, 121 people in South Dakota and Minnesota were struck by a mysterious illness.

A healthy young man dies mysteriously in his sleep and toxicology tests reveal a lethal dose of lidocaine in his blood. Investigators find a suicide note and presume he killed himself until a forensic linguist examines the note.
A murderer eludes the law for years until an age-scaled sculpture helps lead to his arrest.

Survivors of Nazi atrocities recognized Archbishop Trifa, former head of the Romanian Orthodox Church in America, as having directed a bloody attack against Jews during World War II. He was deported in 1984 and died three years later.
After a weekend retreat, a Boy Scout's organs start shutting down, leaving doctors puzzled.
When court clerk Peter Porco doesn't report to work in November 2004, a courts officer is ordered to the Porcos' family home in Bethlehem, NY.
Ten bodies had been found between May and November 1984 in Florida.
The driver said he couldn't have hit and killed a pedestrian on a Harrisburg street. The Jeep Grand Cherokee he was leasing around that time had been sold months ago to a buyer in another state.
A man becomes the prime suspect in the deaths of his parents as police examine mud and blood traces.

When Leann Fletcher is found dead, investigators use blood spatter analysis and forensic computing to find a motive for her murder: her husband, a prominent lawyer, was having an affair with judge Susan Chrzanowski.
The sudden appearance of thick fog causes a 99-car accident on I-75 in Tennessee, killing 12.
When a man is gunned down in his own garage, investigators use science to unravel a twisted tale of lust, greed and deception.
While Earl Morris was vacationing in California, he learned his wife had gone missing.

When a wealthy socialite died after falling down the stairs, witness accounts contradicted evidence. To find out what really happened, investigators employed a physicist and an expert in accident reconstruction.
When a woman exhibits flu-like symptoms before dying, investigators determine she was poisoned.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
In a quiet village in Great Britain, a farmer came upon a chilling sight.

When a woman disappeared without a trace, there were two possible explanations: kidnapping or murder. Careful investigation, a forensic artist and DNA profiling enabled police to find a single suspect, who was known to prey upon vulnerable women.
An infant was rushed to the emergency room with serious breathing problems.
Shortly after daybreak in Vancouver, British Columbia, a fire was set in a dumpster.

When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity. To solve the case, investigators turn to bug larvae found on the body and a tiny wad of chewing gum found near the victim's body.
Two people in Seattle, Washington died after taking an over-the-counter pain reliever.
In 1995, San Diego police are baffled by a pair of hands found in a dumpster. Through further investigation, they determine that the hands are those of missing person Don Hardin.
Evidence reveals a teacher who complained of being stalked by another teacher was scamming police.
When a victim is brutally murdered in his own bed, investigators find a shoe impression in the mud outside — physical evidence they hope will lead to the killer.
On October 15, 1985, two bomb explosions rocked Salt Lake City and resulted in two deaths.

Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a crime scene where one man had been killed and two teenage girls were seriously injured. Neither of the girls could identify their attacker, but one simple clue helped track the footsteps of a killer.
After a day of fishing in a small, quiet village in Switzerland, a teenage boy did not return home.
After being admitted to the hospital with unexplained bleeding, 11-month-old Chad Shelton dies. Investigators and scientists frantically search for a cause when others from the same house fall ill.
Heavy rains and snow run-off carried manure into Milwaukee's water supply in 1993.
Paul Gruber's daughter suspected something was wrong when she received birthday cards addressed from her father, but written in a stranger's handwriting.
Eleven-month-old Chad Shelton was admitted to the hospital with unexplained bleeding and later died.
When the number and volume of bloodstains at the scene was greater than usual, it was up to forensic scientists to find out why.
In the mid-1980s, bodies of nude women were found on a remote hill of California.

Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity. But technology and behavioral science combine to give police a new forensic tool. Police narrow their search to one man: local policeman Randy Comeaux.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a boy scout camp near Farmington, Missouri.

When Scott Dunn goes missing, police spray his bedroom with Luminol and uncover a scene of horrific violence. Now investigators face a daunting task: proving that Scott Dunn had been murdered without a body, a witness or a murder weapon.
A serial bomber was waging a vendetta against the legal profession.

In 2007, the Florida mobile home of Effie and Michael Ratley catches fire. Michael heroically rescues his wife and infant son. A month later, his wife is found beaten to death in a bedroom of his parents' home.
Robert Sims returned home and found his wife, Paula, unconscious on the kitchen floor.
A Modesto, California teenager goes missing. With no signs of struggle in her home, police suspect she has simply run away — until her naked, bruised body is discovered in a ditch 20 miles away.
Forensic scientists re-examine a death previously ruled accidental.
In 1992, 22-year-old Dawn Bruce is brutally murdered in her Virginia apartment. Investigators notice a blood smear on a pillow case that appears to have been made by one of the killer's fingers.
Detectives learn a genetic disorder caused children's deaths, overturning their mother's conviction.
In 1992, Laura Houghteling disappeared from her Bethesda home and was never seen again.

In 1990, Shirley Andronowich's body was found mutilated. Eyewitnesses told police she had a fight with her husband the night before, but forensic evidence proved that he had nothing to do with her death.
The use of DNA testing helps exonerate a person accused of raping a young Virginia woman.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon in April 2002 after he planned to end their relationship.
In 1984, eight-year-old Vicki Hoskins left home to mail a letter for her mother. She never returned.

The woman had been sexually assaulted, stabbed repeatedly and left for dead. When a perfect suspect practically turned himself in, police were sure they had their man — until DNA evidence proved them wrong.
A mother with Munchausen syndrome by proxy kills one child and physically abuses another.
The victim had been stabbed more than thirty times and the crime scene was awash with her blood. Near her head, police discovered a distinctive button with strands of thread still attached.
In 1993, Rose Larner stopped in a convenience store and was never seen or heard from again.

The body of a wealthy American businessman was found in his rental car. Teeth and bone fragments were the only remains. When the victim's wife files an insurance claim for $7 million, investigators seek the help of a renowned forensic anthropologist.
The apparently motiveless murders of two children baffle police.

Residents of Noel, Missouri were stunned to learn that their bank had been robbed and the bank president was missing. His body was later found floating in a lake, securely bound to a chair with duct tape.
A routine missing persons report leads to a deadly love triangle and a murder charge.
In 1991, when the wife of a serviceman was brutally murdered in the Philippines, investigators had to reassemble a tiny computer disk that had been cut to pieces in order to find the killer.

A 1995 fire razes the mansion of a Kansas doctor, killing two of her three children.

A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial. An expert witness has a different opinion as to how the fire started and, if proven, would clear the woman of any culpability.
